clue.text: European bridge is hated, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a span is the arch or stretch of a bridge
taken as written
the opening letter of hated

explanation.surface: A continental card game of bridge is resented from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge suggests the card game, but here it is a structure spanning a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a person from a country in southwestern Europe, so the adjective names one kind of European.

clue.text: Regularly burps after vegetables with duck as a starter

a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A diner belches after eating vegetables with duck to begin the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is often served as the first course of a meal, an appetiser or starter.

clue.text: Aristocrat goes round in flannel bonnet

something that goes round turns back on itself, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the tail of flannel and the start of bonnet

explanation.surface: A lord wanders about wearing a woolly cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a person of high rank by birth or title, a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Drink alcohol for comfort

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink to console themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Support as a noun is emotional help and encouragement, which is solace or comfort.

clue.text: Pressing need to entreat US city to restrict carbon

blocks.note: to urge is to plead with someone
NY is New York
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Someone desperately begs an American city to cut its carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgency is the quality of demanding immediate attention, a synonym for a pressing need or exigency.

clue.text: Refuse to upset sister

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declines to annoy their sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand or decline to comply, so it means to refuse to give in.

clue.text: Moving point by a Liberal in support of proposal

taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician makes a point while backing a motion in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, A and L sit below MOTION, which follows E.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in the sense of stirring deep feelings, as touching or affecting things are emotional.

clue.text: Denounce criminal men behind trick with diamonds

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick

taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Crooks stand behind a jewel swindle and should be publicly censured.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn is to express strong public disapproval, censuring someone, which is what denouncing means.

clue.text: Wholly splendid wild nights to stop — enjoyment never lasts

annotation.answer: ALL GOOD THINGS COME TO AN END

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all means wholly, entirely
good as a synonym for fine, splendid
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabulous wild nights out must eventually cease, as pleasure is always fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says every pleasant experience eventually finishes, so happiness is never permanent.

clue.text: The French finally acclaim British meat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: la is French for the (feminine)
the closing letter of acclaim
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: French diners at last praise British meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the flesh of a young sheep eaten as food, one example of meat.

clue.text: Recovers tug undamaged with queen inside

blocks.note: to tug is to pull
sound means intact, in good condition
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A tugboat comes through unscathed with a queen on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Regina (Latin for queen) gives R, as in ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull round is an idiom meaning to regain health or consciousness after illness, just as a patient recovers.

clue.text: See 9
Spread rumours about spies and dog

blocks.note: the letters of spies and dog together, and dropped

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle circulated concerning secret agents and their dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip is to chat idly about others' private affairs, passing on hearsay and tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Father returns with amount to share out

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word for father is read backwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a portion is a quantity or amount

explanation.surface: Dad comes back with a sum of money to divide among the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to divide and allocate something among several people, distributing it in shares.

clue.text: Floods on top of floating ice sheets reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound of the phrase counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: over means above, on top of
floes are sheets of floating ice

explanation.surface: Melting water spills across the drifting ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that overflows spills over its banks, which is what happens when it floods the land.

clue.text: See 9
Remains like he is

blocks.note: as means in the manner of, like
he is contracts to he's

explanation.surface: A man's remains are described as being just like him.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun for what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the powdery residue left after cremation, so they are a person's mortal remains.

clue.text: Eccentric king abandons foreigner finally

blocks.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An odd monarch leaves an outsider behind at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' says the R removed is the last letter of STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or peculiar, unusual behaviour being exactly what an eccentric shows.

clue.text: Induce badly mutilated son to take over from daughter

indicators.note: badly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters are jumbled
to take over from means one thing steps into another's place, replacing it

blocks.note: taken as written before the swap
S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a son taking his sister's place after she is injured.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the D of MUTILATED for S to get MUTILATES, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to provoke or bring about a reaction or activity, which is what inducing something does.

clue.text: Manages to create second party

blocks.note: to make is to create
S is the abbreviation for second
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in organising a second celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is an idiom for getting by with whatever is available, coping or managing.

clue.text: King Lear, for example, got old beset by trial

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: a try is an attempt or trial
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's old king aged under the weight of his ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a summary of the play itself.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great plays ending in catastrophe, a classic example of the dramatic genre.

clue.text: I'm backing bishop over introduction of recycled glass

the opening letter of recycled

explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title; an over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O.

clue.text: Writing on the wall for tennis player having seizure at international

a fit is a seizure or convulsion

explanation.surface: An omen for a tennis star who collapses at an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing on the wall usually means a sign of doom, which fits the surface story; here it is taken literally. 'having' and 'at' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are words or drawings scrawled or sprayed onto walls in public places, literally markings on walls.

clue.text: Snatch extremely interrupted sleep at the end of work

the first and last letters of interrupted

explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of interrupted and a nap come after the last letter of work.

clue.text: Was bold enough to disturb adder

clue.text: Boosts national spirit during enemy shelling at first

spirit in the sense of bravery, mettle
the opening letter of shelling

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
taken as written
sure means certain

clue.text: I'm off to travel round Germany via Spain

O is a round shape
